title: Response to Welcome (World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago)

access.edition_or_version: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, vol. 1; contemporary newspaper reports

mechanics.premise: Addressing an international assembly of religions, the speaker reframes a history of sectarian violence as a forward call for tolerance and mutual recognition.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Warm greeting and gratitude give way to plain naming of sectarian harm and then to a forward hope for its end.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Direct address that converts strangers into kin, anaphora of gratitude and of identity, embedded hymn and scriptural reference, antithesis of past fanaticism and future fellowship.
mechanics.dialogue: Spoken to a live multi-faith audience, with the rhetoric of a welcome returned.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person singular representing a collective ('millions of Hindu people').
mechanics.tone_relevant_techniques: Verbal persuasion of collective capability (self-efficacy); civic-prophetic indictment-then-promise; performative direct address; Indian civic uplift on an international stage.
mechanics.critical_reception: Treated as a landmark of interreligious dialogue and a defining moment of modern Indian public rhetoric.
